Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:10:1.english: He grew his hair and his fingernails - He grew his hair and his fingernails to disfigure himself [in order] to repent.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:12:1.english: Where they do not recognize him - For repentance there is not [an act of] deception.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:12:2.hebrew: ויחזיר אבידה - אם ימצא אבידת חבירו, דכיון דמחזיר אבידה הוא, ודאי הדר ביה מחמדת ממון:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:12:2.english: And returns a lost item - If he finds his fellow's lost item, for since he returns a lost item, he has certainly repented of [his] desire for money.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:13:1.hebrew: אם תקדמיה יונך ליון - ליוני, אתן לך כך וכך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:13:1.english: If your pigeon outpaces [my] pigeon - [Meaning,] to my pigeon; [then] I will give you such and such.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:13:2.hebrew: ארא - אשתליו"ן, מלומד להביא יונים ממקומן לבית בעלים על כרחן, ויש בהן גזל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:13:2.english: An ara - Estalion [a decoy bird], trained to bring pigeons from their place to [its] owner's house against their will, and there is [an element of] robbery in them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:15:1.hebrew: מפני דרכי שלום בעלמא - דתניא (חולין דף קמא:): "יוני שובך ויוני עלייה — יש בהן גזל מפני דרכי שלום", ולא גזל גמור, דלא זכה בהן בעל השובך, דממילא קאתו ורבו להתם. ובגמרא דהשואל (דף קב.) גרס לה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:15:1.english: Merely due to the ways of peace - For it is taught in a baraita (Chullin 141b): “Pigeons of a dovecote and pigeons of an attic are subject to the prohibition of robbery on account of the ways of peace” — and not full-fledged robbery, for the owner of the dovecote did not acquire them, since they came and grew up there on their own. And in the Gemara of the chapter HaSho’el (102a), this is the reading:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:18:1.hebrew: תנא תולה בדעת עצמו - דהויא אסמכתא, והדר תנא דתולה בדעת יונו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:18:1.english: [The Tanna] taught [one who] depends on his own decision - Which is an asmachta, and then taught [one] who depends on the decision of his pigeon.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:1:1.hebrew: אימתי ובמה - "אימתי" — כגון במתניתין דהכא, או "במה דברים אמורים":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:1:1.english: “When” and “in what [case]” - “When” — such as in our Mishnah here; or “In what case is this statement said?”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:3:1.hebrew: גברא אגברא - דרבי יהושע בן לוי ארמי בר חמא? רמי בר חמא סבר: אימתי דרבי יהודה לחלוק בא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:3:1.english: [One] man against [another] man - [Are you setting the statement] of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi against [that of] Rami bar Ḥama? Rami bar Ḥama holds: [The term] “When” of Rabbi Yehuda comes to disagree.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:5:1.hebrew: ההיא דרבי יהודה היא משום רבי טרפון - לעולם "אימתי" לפרש הוא, ורבנן דמתניתין לא פליגי עליה. ומתניתא דקתני "בין שיש לו כו'", דמשמע טעמא משום אסמכתא — ר' יהודה גופיה אמרה משמיה דרבי טרפון, ופליג אדרבנן דמתניתין, דטעמייהו משום יישוב. ובמתניתין, ר' יהודה מילתייהו דרבנן קא מפרש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:5:1.english: That [baraita] is of Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Tarfon - In truth, [the phrase] "When [does this apply]" is [stated] to clarify, and the Rabbis of the mishna do not disagree with him. And the baraita that teaches: "Whether he has [another occupation], etc.," which implies that the reason [he is disqualified] is because of asmakhta — Rabbi Yehuda himself stated it in the name of Rabbi Tarfon, and [Rabbi Tarfon] disagrees with the Rabbis of the mishna, whose reason is because of [not contributing to the] settlement [of the world]; and in the mishna, Rabbi Yehuda was [merely] explaining the words of the Rabbis.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:5:2.hebrew: אין אחד מהן נזיר - שנים יושבין ואחד עובר. זה אומר: "פלוני העובר נזיר הוא", וזה אומר: "אינו נזיר". ואמר אחד: "הריני נזיר אם כמותו הוא — שהוא נזיר", וחבירו אומר: "הריני נזיר אם כמותו הוא — שאינו נזיר", ושניהם מתכוונין לנזירות, ונמצא כאחד מהם. ואמר רבי טרפון: "אין אחד מהן נזיר", שעל הספק אמר דבריו תחילה, ואין זו הפלאה — ד"כי יפליא איש" (ויקרא כז), "יפרש" משמע. אלמא לר' טרפון, דכי תלי תנאה במידי דלאו בידיה ולא ידע לה — אפילו הכי הויא אסמכתא, ולא אמרינן מספיקא גמר ואקני:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:5:2.english: Neither of them is a nazirite - Two [people] were sitting and one was passing by. This one says: “So-and-so who is passing by is a nazirite,” and that one says: “He is not a nazirite.” And one said: “Behold, I am a nazirite if it is as he says — that he is a nazirite,” and his fellow says: “Behold, I am a nazirite if it is as he says — that he is not a nazirite.” And both of them intend [to commit to] naziriteship, and [the matter] was found to be like one of them. And Rabbi Tarfon said: “Neither of them is a nazirite,” for he uttered his words initially in [a state of] uncertainty, and this is not an explicit declaration [hafla’ah] — as “when a man shall clearly utter” (Leviticus 27[:2]) means “he shall express clearly.” Consequently, according to Rabbi Tarfon, when one hinges a condition on something that is not in his control and he does not know [the outcome], even so it is an asmakhta, and we do not say that out of uncertainty he conclusively resolved to transfer [ownership].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:6:1.hebrew: לוה בריבית פסול לעדות - דקיי"ל (ב"מ דף עה:): המלוה והלוה עוברין בלא תעשה. וכיון דחימוד ממון מעבירו על דת, הוה לי' כרשע דחמס, דעובר נמי על לא תעשה מפני חימוד ממון:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:6:1.english: One who borrows with interest is disqualified from bearing witness - For it is established for us (Bava Metzia 75b) that the lender and the borrower violate a negative commandment. And since the coveting of money causes him to transgress the law, he is considered like a wicked person of illicit gain [rasha dechamas], who also violates a negative commandment because of the coveting of money.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:6:2.english: A loan that comes with interest - And [this] implies both of them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:7:1.english: Bar Binittos - [The word] ozif [means that he was the] lender.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:8:1.hebrew: והוה ליה - האי סהדא רשע, דהא אודי דלווה בריבית:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:8:1.english: And he is - This witness [is] a wicked person, for he admitted that he borrowed with interest.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:9:1.hebrew: רבא לטעמיה - בפ"ק, דאין אדם משים עצמו כו' — אינו יכול לפסול עצמו על פיו, דהא אין קרוב מעיד, לא לזכות ולא לחובה, ואדם קרוב אצל עצמו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a:9:1.english: Rava [conforms] to his line of reasoning - In the first chapter, [where it says] that "a person does not make himself [wicked]," etc. — he cannot disqualify himself by his own admission, for a relative does not testify, neither to acquit nor to convict, and a person is a relative to himself.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25a:5:1.hebrew: ההיא ר' יהודה משום ר' טרפון - דאמר: "לא נתנה נזירות אלא להפלאה". פ"ה: אלמא כיון דמספקא ליה אי הוי נזיר אי לא — מספיקא לא משעביד נפשיה; הכא נמי, מספיקא לא גמר ומקני. והקשה הריב"ן: מאי מדמה קנין לנזירות? שאני נזירות דגלי קרא, דכתיב: "כי יפליא"! וי"ל: דמ"מ נילף מיניה בעלמא. ור"י פי': דמ"מ מייתי שפיר, ואין להקשות "שאני הכא דגלי קרא" — משום דהא לא מפרש בקרא מאי היא הפלאה, אלא גלי לן קרא דבעינן הפלאה, ולא ידעינן מה היא הפלאה, אלא תיתי לן מסברא מה היא הפלאה. והיינו דקאמר: "ההיא רבי יהודה היא דאמר משום רבי טרפון" — דכיון דלא חשיב ליה הפלאה, א"כ ש"מ דעל כרחיך הוא דאמר לעיל בכי האי גוונא אסמכתא היא; דאי לאו אסמכתא היא מילתא דלא ידע, אם כן הויא נמי הך הפלאה אע"ג דלא ידע. ומדקאמר ר' יהודה: "לעולם אין אחד מהם נזיר וכו'" — מכלל דלא הוי הפלאה כי האי גוונא; אם כן ש"מ לעיל דהוי אסמכתא כי האי גוונא. וקרא ד"כי יפליא" איצטריך משום דידות נזירות כנזירות; הלכך אי לאו קרא ד"כי יפליא", הייתי מרבה גם זו לידות נזירות, דלא גרע מהם; ומשום הכי איצטריך "כי יפליא", לומר דלא חשיב כידות:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 25a:5:1.english: "That is Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Tarfon" - Who said [in the baraita that] naziriteship was given only for explicitness [i.e., when uttered with certainty]. Rashi explained: Evidently, since it is uncertain to him whether he is a nazirite or not, he does not obligate himself out of uncertainty; here too [in gambling with dice], out of uncertainty he does not wholeheartedly resolve to transfer ownership. And the Rivan objected: Why compare an acquisition [of money] to naziriteship? Naziriteship is different, as Scripture revealed [that it requires certainty], as it is written: "When [a man] shall clearly utter [a vow of a nazirite]" (Numbers 6:2)! And one can say that nevertheless, we derive from it [a general principle] elsewhere [that a person does not commit oneself under uncertainty]. And the Ri explained that nevertheless, [the Gemara] brings [the proof] well, and one should not object: "It is different here because Scripture revealed it" — because Scripture does not explain what constitutes explicitness (hafla'ah); rather, Scripture revealed to us [only] that we require explicitness, but we would not know what constitutes explicitness except that it should come to us by reason [to determine] what constitutes explicitness. And this is what [the Gemara] means by saying: "That is Rabbi Yehuda who said in the name of Rabbi Tarfon" — for since he did not consider this [case of uncertainty] to be explicitness, if so, conclude from this that perforce it is he who said above [on 24b] that in such a case it is an asmakhta; for if a matter that one does not know were not an asmakhta, then this [vow] would also be considered explicitness even though he does not know. And from the fact that Rabbi Yehuda said: "Actually, neither of them is a nazirite, etc.", by inference in such a case it is not explicitness; if so, conclude from this [with regard to the discussion] above that in such a case it is an asmakhta. And the verse "when he clearly utters" was necessary because [ordinarily] allusions (yadot) to naziriteship are like naziriteship; therefore, were it not for the verse "when he clearly utters", I would have included this [case] as well among allusions to naziriteship, as it is no worse than them; and because of this, "when he clearly utters" was necessary, to state that it is not considered an allusion.
